product.name: swift-design-system
product.purpose: Provide reusable, strongly typed design-system mechanics for Apple-platform apps while keeping each consuming app's visual vocabulary and product semantics app-owned.

primary_users.technical_level: Experienced Swift developer working across SwiftUI and native UIKit/AppKit surfaces.
primary_users.work_context: Builds multiple Apple-platform applications that should share design-system mechanics without sharing app-specific token vocabularies or visual identity.

jobs_to_be_done.statement: Reuse design-system mechanics across Apple apps without coupling the package to any one app's semantic vocabulary or visual identity.
Represent app-owned design decisions with finite Swift token vocabularies and compiler-known symbols rather than strings or runtime dictionaries.
Resolve scalar design tokens synchronously to native Apple layout value types without wrapper-unwrapping boilerplate.
Enumerate and validate complete app-owned token vocabularies through public capability interfaces using DesignSystemTestSupport.

must_reduce: Repeated per-app implementation of shared design-system mechanics.
Stringly typed or runtime-only token lookup.
Cross-app drift in design-system conventions and framework adaptation.
Boilerplate required to consume design values from SwiftUI, UIKit, and AppKit.
Duplicated app-specific validation infrastructure for finite token vocabularies.
must_not_become: A repository of app-specific palettes, spacing scales, semantic token names, fonts, assets, or branding.
A monolithic universal design-token abstraction that pre-models unrelated future token families.
A runtime token dictionary or string-keyed lookup system.
A package-owned global current design system or runtime theme state object.
A multi-product architecture split into separate Core, SwiftUI, UIKit, and AppKit libraries.
A source of production scalar-value sanitization or hidden mutation of app-authored scalar capability results.
experience_principles: Prefer small capability-specific public seams over speculative abstractions.
Keep app token vocabularies and aggregate design-system values app-owned.
Return native Apple framework value types where wrappers add no leverage.
Make lookup synchronous, deterministic, side-effect-free, nonthrowing, and cheap.
Use compile-time structure and finite CaseIterable vocabularies instead of runtime identity systems.
Keep Swift 6 strict-concurrency compatibility without unnecessary main-actor isolation.
Validate through public capability seams rather than private implementation structure.
